basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 6.' and it opens 'Vers. 6. Erat autem Joseph pulchra facie. Joseph diximus Christum significare, cujus'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 6. Erat autem Joseph pulchra facie. Joseph diximus Christum significare, cujus pulchritudo omnem superexcellit formositatem, de qua Psalmista: Speciosus forma prae filiis hominum (Psal. XLIV, 3). Et Apostolus: In quem de iderant angeli prospicere (I Petr. I, 12). Ipse revera prospere in omnibus agit, et omnia in manu illius diriguntur.
